title: Universal filtration truncations and their distinguished triangles
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with localizations taken in a common larger universe. Let $DF^+(\mathcal C)$ be the localization of bounded-below cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with a finite decreasing filtration by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] at maps that are quasi-isomorphisms on every graded complex. Finite means that $F^aM=M$ and $F^{b+1}M=0$ for some integers $a\le b$, independently of cochain degree. This localization has the triangulated structure [def-weil-triangulated-category] induced by filtered mapping cones. Forgetting the filtration $\omega:DF^+(\mathcal C)\to D^+(\mathcal C)$ and each graded-piece functor $\operatorname{gr}^p:DF^+(\mathcal C)\to D^+(\mathcal C)$ are exact.

For every integer $r$, the subcomplex truncation $t_{\ge r}M=F^rM$ and quotient truncation $t_{<r}M=M/F^rM$, with induced and quotient filtrations, descend to exact functors. They have graded pieces respectively $\operatorname{gr}^pM$ for $p\ge r$ and $p<r$, and zero otherwise. Write $DF^{+,\ge r}$ and $DF^{+,<r}$ for the full subcategories whose graded pieces vanish for $p<r$ and $p\ge r$, respectively. There is a natural distinguished triangle $t_{\ge r}M\xrightarrow{\iota_{r,M}}M\xrightarrow{q_{r,M}}t_{<r}M\to(t_{\ge r}M)[1]$, induced by the subcomplex inclusion and quotient. It is uniquely determined, up to unique isomorphism inducing the identity on $M$, among distinguished triangles $L\to M\to R\to L[1]$ with $L\in DF^{+,\ge r}$ and $R\in DF^{+,<r}$.

For $L\in DF^{+,\ge r}$ and $R\in DF^{+,<r}$, the canonical maps $\operatorname{Hom}(L,t_{\ge r}M)\xrightarrow{\iota_{r,M}\circ -}\operatorname{Hom}(L,M)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(t_{<r}M,R)\xrightarrow{-\circ q_{r,M}}\operatorname{Hom}(M,R)$ are bijective, naturally in their arguments. Thus $t_{\ge r}$ is right adjoint to the inclusion of $DF^{+,\ge r}$, and $t_{<r}$ is left adjoint to the inclusion of $DF^{+,<r}$.

Put $T_p=t_{\ge p}t_{<p+1}$. This functor has only the graded piece $\operatorname{gr}^pM$, and $\omega T_p=\operatorname{gr}^p$ canonically and naturally. On the full subcategory with all other graded pieces zero, the truncation maps identify $T_p$ with the identity, and forgetting filtration is an equivalence to $D^+(\mathcal C)$, inverse to placing a complex in filtration degree $p$. All assertions use vanishing in the derived category, so apply even when the other graded complexes are acyclic rather than literally zero.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal K$ be the category of bounded-below complexes with a uniform finite filtration, modulo filtration-preserving homotopies. Filtered-homotopic maps $f\simeq g:X\to Y$, $f-g=dh+hd$, already agree in $DF^+(\mathcal C)$: the filtered cylinder $\operatorname{Cyl}X^n=X^n\oplus X^{n+1}\oplus X^n$, $d(a,b,c)=(da-b,-db,dc+b)$, with direct-sum filtration, has inclusions $i_0,i_1$ of the outer summands, a common retraction $p(a,b,c)=a+c$ which is a filtered homotopy equivalence (hence a graded quasi-isomorphism), and $f=\varphi i_0$, $g=\varphi i_1$ for $\varphi=f\,\mathrm{pr}_1-h\,\mathrm{pr}_2+g\,\mathrm{pr}_3$; so $Q(i_0)=Q(p)^{-1}=Q(i_1)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], $DF^+(\mathcal C)$ is the localization of $\mathcal K$ at the graded quasi-isomorphisms $W$. The objects of $\mathcal K$ form a full subcategory of the cone-triangulated $K^+$ of finite filtered objects [lem-trf-filtered-cone-localization] closed under zero, shifts (same bounds) and cones (bounds $[\min a,\max b]$), so $\mathcal K$ is triangulated by the cone triangles [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. Let $\mathcal P\subseteq\mathcal K$ be the graded-acyclic complexes. It contains $0$ and is stable under shifts and filtered homotopy equivalences. Given a distinguished $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ with $K,M\in\mathcal P$, its rotation $M[-1]\to K\to L$ is isomorphic to a cone triangle $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\to C(u)$ with $X,Y\in\mathcal P$; each $\operatorname{gr}^pu$ is a map of acyclic complexes, so $u\in W$ and the cone criterion of [lem-trf-filtered-cone-localization] gives $L\simeq C(u)\in\mathcal P$. By that criterion $W=W_{\mathcal P}$, so [lem-trf-triangulated-subcategory-cone-system] gives a multiplicative system with both calculi of fractions compatible with the triangulation, and [lem-pur-localization-triangles-05r6] makes $DF^+(\mathcal C)$ triangulated, with distinguished triangles those isomorphic to images of cone triangles and $Q$ exact.

The operations $t_{\ge r}K=F^rK$ and $t_{<r}K=K/F^rK$ with induced and quotient filtrations [def-sp-filtration] are additive on $\mathcal K$: a filtration-preserving homotopy restricts to $F^r$ and descends to $K/F^r$. They commute with shifts and with mapping cones and their direct-sum filtrations, $F^rC(u)=C(F^ru)$ and $C(u)/F^r=C(u/F^r)$. Since $F^p(F^rK)=F^{\max(p,r)}K$ and $F^p(K/F^rK)=F^{\min(p,r)}K/F^rK$, their graded complexes [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] are $\operatorname{gr}^pK$ for $p\ge r$ (zero otherwise) and $\operatorname{gr}^pK$ for $p<r$ (zero otherwise). So each graded map of a truncated $s\in W$ is $\operatorname{gr}^p(s)$ or a map of zero complexes; truncations preserve $W$ and descend by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. They send cone triangles to cone triangles, hence are exact for the triangulation of Step 1. For $\omega$: the sequences $0\to F^{p+1}K\to F^pK\to\operatorname{gr}^pK\to0$ are degreewise exact by definition of $\operatorname{gr}^p$; for a graded quasi-isomorphism $s:K\to K'$, take a common interval $F^a=$ everything, $F^{b+1}=0$, and descend from $p=b+1$ to $p=a$ with the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] and the five lemma, to get that $F^ps$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every $p$, in particular $\omega s=F^as$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Filtered homotopies forget to homotopies, so $\omega$ descends; $\operatorname{gr}^p$ descends by definition of $W$. Both preserve shifts and cones literally, so they are exact.

For the inclusion $\iota:F^rM\hookrightarrow M$, form its filtered mapping cone. In grade $p<r$ the induced map is $0\to\operatorname{gr}^pM$, so the cone-to-quotient map is the identity onto $\operatorname{gr}^p(M/F^rM)$. In grade $p\ge r$ the induced map is $\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{gr}^pM}$, so its cone is contractible and the quotient grade is zero. Thus the cone maps by a graded quasi-isomorphism to $M/F^rM$; the cone-localization result makes this the distinguished triangle $t_{\ge r}M\to M\to t_{<r}M\to(t_{\ge r}M)[1]$. The same calculation gives the stated graded-piece formula. It also shows directly that the triangle is natural for chain maps, hence for localized maps after descent.

Let $L\in DF^{+,\ge r}$ and $R\in DF^{+,<r}$, represented by complexes. By the graded-piece formula of Step 2, $t_{\ge r}L\to L$ and $R\to t_{<r}R$ are graded quasi-isomorphisms (on the other grades they relate $0$ and an acyclic graded complex), so assume $F^rL=L$ and $F^rR=0$ literally. Orthogonality: by Step 1 and [lem-pc-right-fraction-representation] a morphism $Q(L)\to Q(R[q])$ is $Q(f)Q(s)^{-1}$ with $s:Z\to L$ in $W$ and $f:Z\to R[q]$ in $\mathcal K$. As $t_{<r}L=0$ and $t_{<r}$ preserves $W$, $t_{<r}Z$ is graded acyclic. By Step 3 the cone of $a:t_{\ge r}Z\to Z$ maps by a graded quasi-isomorphism to $t_{<r}Z$, so it is graded acyclic and $a\in W$ by the cone criterion of [lem-trf-filtered-cone-localization]. Then $Q(f)Q(s)^{-1}=Q(fa)Q(sa)^{-1}$, and the filtered map $fa$ sends $F^rZ$, its whole source, into $F^r(R[q])=0$. Hence $\operatorname{Hom}(L,R[q])=0$ for all $q$. Hom bijections: by (TR1) and (TR2) of [def-weil-triangulated-category], $L\xrightarrow1L\to0\to L[1]$ and $0\to R\xrightarrow1R\to0$ are distinguished (the latter rotates to $R\xrightarrow1R\to0\to R[1]$). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-triangle-morphism-extension] to the first triangle and the triangle of Step 3 with middle map $g:L\to M$: $q_{r,M}g\in\operatorname{Hom}(L,t_{<r}M)=0$, so (1) gives $f$ with $\iota_{r,M}f=g$, unique by (2) as $\operatorname{Hom}(L[1],t_{<r}M)=0$. Apply it to the triangle of Step 3 and the second triangle with middle map $g:M\to R$: $g\iota_{r,M}\in\operatorname{Hom}(t_{\ge r}M,R)=0$ gives $h$ with $hq_{r,M}=g$, unique as $\operatorname{Hom}((t_{\ge r}M)[1],R)=0$. Both bijections are composition with fixed maps, so natural in $L$, $R$, and in $M$ by naturality of the triangle; this is the right- and left-adjoint assertion.

proof.text: Let $L\to M\to R\to L[1]$ be any distinguished triangle with $L$ high-supported and $R$ low-supported. The composite $L\to M\to t_{<r}M$ is zero by the vanishing in Step 4, so the generic morphism-of-triangles extension lemma [lem-weil-pbc-triangle-morphism-extension] gives a morphism from this triangle to the canonical truncation triangle whose middle component is $1_M$. The same vanishing after every shift gives $\operatorname{Hom}(L[1],t_{<r}M)=0$, so the first and third components are unique. Reversing the two triangles produces a morphism in the opposite direction; the composites extend $1_M$ and are therefore identities by the same uniqueness. Thus the comparison is a unique isomorphism fixing $M$. The inclusion and quotient maps are consequently the unique maps characterized by the two Hom bijections, which also proves functoriality and uniqueness of the triangle.

For $T_p=t_{\ge p}t_{<p+1}$, applying the graded-piece formula twice leaves exactly $\operatorname{gr}^pM$ and kills every other grade. On complexes, $\omega T_pM=F^pM/F^{p+1}M=\operatorname{gr}^pM$, and this identification is natural. Place an ordinary bounded-below complex $N$ in filtration degree $p$; the resulting functor $J_p:D^+(\mathcal C)\to DF^+(\mathcal C)$ is exact, and $\omega J_p=1$. If all other graded pieces of $M$ vanish in the derived category, the truncation maps are graded quasi-isomorphisms onto the degree-$p$ representative, so $M\simeq J_p(\operatorname{gr}^pM)$ and $T_pM\simeq M$. Conversely $J_p(N)$ has no other graded piece. Thus $J_p$ and forgetting filtration are quasi-inverse on the pure-grade subcategory, and all claims remain valid when the other grades are acyclic rather than literally zero because the localization inverts exactly graded quasi-isomorphisms.
